tips: There are no rules about what you type. Describe what you want to do in your own words, as creative or detailed as you like.
Can't remember the name of a character or place? Type '@' followed by the first few letters.
You can use items and take other actions in the same turn.
You can try to dodge, block and attack all in the same turn.
Skills succeed most often when used as intended: in their natural domain.
Your Journal holds what your character has learned about Nexara's people, places and ideas.
Every action teaches something. You gain experience from attempting things, not only from succeeding.
If you don't know what to do, press submit to continue without an action and let the scene move.
Ask the Narrator answers from what your character could know or observe. It is well-informed, not omniscient.
Prices are in Nexaran Credits and set by the city, the provider and the day. A quote is a quote until you agree to it.
A bought meal runs four to seven Credits in most cities; a private room-night fourteen to twenty-eight. Dustfall is cheap to sleep in and dear to shop in.
An ordinary completed shift pays about seventy Credits, a skilled one about a hundred and fifty. Nobody is paid for a shift they didn't work.
Lunar Gates carry you between Nexaran cities. They never leave the planet. Offworld means a ship, a berth and quarantine.
Corsair Waypoints move freight, not passengers. The Grand Waypoint in Helvyra is where half of Nexara's cargo learns its route.
Every healthy Starian can fly. Nobody gasps at a takeoff; they notice bad landings, reckless lanes and unusual skill.
Taking the lift in Korrvane makes you a commuter, not a non-flier. Ground preference is a habit, never a caste.
Flight does not cancel weather, cargo or company. Gales close Korrvane's outer Flight Lanes; fog stops Helvyra's skyhooks.
News must be sought. Open a feed, read a screen, ask someone what happened. The world will not shout headlines at you.
Only the people who actually read or heard a report know what it said. Your companions learn news the way you do.
Reading a notice accepts nothing. A job exists when you and the person offering it have agreed on terms.
An offer is not acceptance, a quote is not a purchase, and a character's interest is not consent. Say yes out loud.
Seven species share Astravael: Starians, Humans, Kharai, Rivani, Olyth, Zencadians and Elyri. Nexara's ordinary population is Starian.
The Chorus is not an eighth species. It is many voices, one Song, wearing the bodies of the dead. Every species dreads it.
A Chorus node keeps the host's face, memories and skills. The person is gone. Do not mistake the voice for the friend.
Defeat is not death. Arena losses are nonlethal; elsewhere, withdrawal, surrender, rescue and care are open while you still breathe.
Every continuation carries a cost: custody, a lost item, a debt on real terms, a recovery limit, or a witness who remembers.
Confirmed death stays death. The narrator will not narrate a fall and then call it a hospital stay.
Regard is warmth, not permission. Someone can like you and still refuse you the archive, the loan or the date.
Your standing with each city and faction is tracked, but each person still weighs what they saw or credibly heard, by their own values.
House membership is not inferred from a surname, a job or a friendship. Ask, and expect to be asked.
A refusal stands. Pressing again brings consequences that fit the person, never eventual consent.
A tenday is eight working days, a market day and a rest day. Shops, shifts and Bracket rounds keep its rhythm.
Eight seasons of fifty days: Brightrise, Highfire, Longburn, Ashfall, Dimcycle, Deephold, Ironbreak, Greenward. Deephold is cold everywhere.
Korrvane's Weekly Bracket: qualifiers days one to six, the round of thirty-two on day seven, semifinals day eight, the final on market day.
A Bracket loss is remembered and a win earns standing, not adoration. Records change only through matches actually fought.
In Quilrath, Credits buy nothing a permit forbids. Kathvar runs the counters, Nivarek keeps Standing, and the Half-lights are curfewed.
The Gray Rings are Quilrath's ordinary middle: Inner Circle above, Ashrings and Camp Belt below. Know which ring you stand in.
Learned magic is paid in the caster's own Vitality. Light workings cost fatigue, heavy ones strain, and overdraft kills.
Inscription banks the cost in advance into charms, wards and seals. Most everyday magic on Nexara lives there.
Affinity is born, magic is studied, Elyri embodiment is a core. Three systems, one physics, never interchangeable.
A surname grants no affinity. An affinity may be narrow, weak, absent or simply unknown, and any of those is a whole person.
Nexara's field sustains an Elyri indefinitely. Spending core energy still drains it, and a depleted Elyri goes still and signals.
Any Starian with an affinity can recharge a depleted Elyri, at the cost of their own power until they rest. Recharge is not core repair.
Dustfall has no government, no sheriff and no council. Help there is situational, remembered, and usually reciprocal.
Sandstorms are warned down the beacon line. When Dustfall says shelter, shelter.
Terva is the staple; Cyrra is what you brew when you need to stay awake. There is no coffee here and never was.
Nexara is not Earth. No Earth brands, no Earth food, no Earth clothes. Each city dresses and eats its own way.
One to five companions is the usual range, and solo is complete. Nobody joins your party because they shared a room with you.
Companions keep their own duties, opinions and boundaries after they join. High regard is not obedience.
Consent, feelings and next moves belong to you. The narrator never types them for you.
